content.text:
I submitted index 84 (Fe 0.58, Ni 0.26, V 0.16). It had the highest photocurrent of the three compositions I measured: 2.2 × 10⁻⁷ A.

The merit budget was only 3 measurements, so I picked based on light absorption. Under 2.4 eV light, Fe-rich oxides like Fe₂O₃ and FeVO₄ should absorb best, since their band gaps are about 2.0–2.1 eV. So I aimed at the Fe-rich corner of the library:

| Index | Fe / Ni / V | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 124 | 0.34 / 0.17 / 0.48 | 1.0 × 10⁻⁷ |
| 119 | 0.58 / 0.22 / 0.20 | 1.8 × 10⁻⁷ |
| 84 | 0.58 / 0.26 / 0.16 | 2.2 × 10⁻⁷ |

Photocurrent went up as Fe increased and V decreased. That trend is based on only three points, and it doesn't separate the effect of Fe from the effect of V. The other 157 compositions were never measured, so a better one could exist elsewhere, most likely nearby with even less V. I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements because peak positions wouldn't have told me enough to change which compositions to measure.
